Session 6. Executed the session-5 split plan after re-verifying every code fact it rests on against the current tree (no code changes this session - the split is the step):
1. Baseline re-confirmed: `python3 tools/right_place.py --all` -> 324 pairings, 15 flagged (identical to iterations 95/109); queue file {at, entries: 117}; my data area unchanged since fc67bb9 (git diff fc67bb9..HEAD empty for every file I touch; the only post-fc67bb9 delta is the lead's cf29be2 in tools/site_done.py).
2. API verified in tools/right_place.py (696 lines, stdlib): load(root) with all stores optional (none present = no-op), picture_facts(data, plan, row), site_facts(data, site), check_pairing(site, facts) -> (flagged, "same name, other place: <caption place> vs <site place>"), find_right_site(data, facts, exclude, top=3, min_score=0.5) -> [(score, catalog_rec, words)]. The verbatim core spans lines 33-223; its top-level names (US_STATES, ABBR, UK_ABBR, UK_COUNTIES, GENERIC, norm, name_keys, tokens, place_of, site_place, site_toks, name_lookup_keys, row_inputs, score_candidate, BOOK_SCOPE, PLACE_WORDS, phrases = 17; the iteration-95 note's "18 blocks" was a miscount - the marker range plus these names is the contract) all exist at top level in pipeline/books_match.py, whose load_catalog/match_row/_key/main are NOT copied. The 805 drift test compares the 17 blocks by name.
3. Wiring shape fixed in 804's spec: build() is two-phase - every flag decision computed over the PRE-MUTATION candidate sets, then drops/moves/upserts applied, then entries recomputed - so a move into a site cannot feed that site's own flag decision in the same build. Disposition: built right site T -> the row (sites narrowed to [T]) joins T's entry in memory; unbuilt T -> upsert into T's item; no right site -> upsert into the source item (fit/review.upsert_item; imported the way tools/site_done.py imports review, sys.path insert of ROOT/fit). Upserts idempotent-by-value (reason deterministic from stored fields); a flagged candidate already in the source's own item stays out of the queue and is not re-upserted (steady state). A no-picture item that gains a moved first candidate gets renamed to <site>.<plan>.json (upsert_item's lead rule) - called out in the spec.
4. test_fit_queue_real today copies only the four 305 inputs (no catalog/books) -> the check is a no-op in that tree; 804 extends the copy to data/catalog/ + data/books/ (index.jsonl + lists/) and re-derives the expected set WITH the check (the test imports tools/right_place, stdlib). The dead-socket GUARD stays; the checkout must remain byte-identical. data/catalog/sites.jsonl is 6.2 MB, data/books/ 4 MB - copying per test run is fine.
5. Deviation from the session-5 plan (which had both subtasks on `Depends on: 309`): 805 gets `Depends on: 309, 804` - a rebuild with the wired build cannot run before 804 merges, and depending on 309 alone would let the driver hand 805 out early.

The 307a reference's "document in README" line is satisfied there.
7. 804 needs the module commit fc67bb9 (on agent/c, not yet on main): its Notes say so explicitly - a branch without tools/right_place.py waits for 309 to merge rather than rebuilding a copy.

### 2026-10-12 309 DECISION: iteration 98 (session 7) - the split's dependency graph was deadlocking the driver queue; rewrote my own subtasks' lines to the project convention (804: none; 805: 804) and removed the satisfied Depends on: 305
Session 7, no code changes. The driver re-handed 309 (split) while both subtasks sat in Tasks-in-flight (open) but NOT in Next-open-tasks, while the other split's subtasks 207a/207b (both `Depends on: 200`, done) WERE in Next-open-tasks. Diagnosis: I had given 804 `Depends on: 309` and 805 `Depends on: 309, 804` when splitting (session 6, commit 54a9d44). A split parent only becomes done AFTER its subtasks finish (the driver returns it then for the tick work), so a dependency on it can never be satisfied - a deadlock, not a wait (contrast 206, whose deps 211/218 were externally resolvable, so 206's 20 bring-backs were just waiting). Every earlier split in the repo uses the opposite convention - subtasks never depend on the split parent: 203a (001, 200, 201, 202, 802, 803) / 203b (203a); 207a/207b/207c (200); 213a (none) / 213b (213a); 302a (none) / 302b (302a) / 302c (302b) / 302d (302c); 307a (none, a record) / 307b (307a) / 307c (307b) / 307d (307c). The module-availability concern behind my 804->309 edge is handled without it: subtasks run in the parent's owner lane (agent c), whose branch already has fc67bb9 (the module) - the lane assumption is load-bearing, not redundant (verified this session: main head cf29be2, `git cat-file -e main:tools/right_place.py` = absent, so a branch that gets main merged does NOT have the module until 309 merges); both subtasks' Notes now carry the AGENTS.md runtime rule for the case a different agent's branch receives them (add `Depends on: 309` at that point, commit, wait - never copy the module). 805's `Depends on: 309` was pure duplication of its 804 edge (after 804 merges, the chain carries both the wiring and the module) - cut to `Depends on: 804`, which is its real ordering need (the rebuild runs after the wiring merges). Also removed the now-satisfied `Depends on: 305` from 309 itself (305 is done; the 302a precedent: remove satisfied deps from your own line). Authority: AGENTS.md - "Rewrite, reorder (rename the letters), add or drop your subtasks whenever you learn more" - both files are mine and unmodified by anyone since 54a9d44; the lead has precedent for cutting dead edges from the task graph (0be0b09 on 206: "a cycle that kept 206 open") but that is a human-side action I did not need to ask for, because these are my own subtasks' lines and the fix follows the repo's dominant convention. Baseline re-verified in the same session: `python3 tools/right_place.py --all` -> 324 pairings, 15 flagged (identical to iterations 95/109/97), my data area byte-identical since fc67bb9; no test reads tasks/ (grep confirmed), so this change cannot affect the suite. Expected driver behavior after this commit: 804 (Depends on: none) enters Next-open-tasks and is handed out in order - to agent c, whose branch has the module; 805 follows when 804 merges; when both are done the driver returns 309 and I tick its three carved boxes and set it done.

### 2026-10-12 309 DECISION: iteration 99 (session 8) - the driver re-handed 309, so I started 804 in the owner lane: the refactor-first step landed (build() gathers per-site candidate maps, entries via the new _entry(); behavior-neutral, proven by an old-vs-new run on one tree); the two-phase wiring is the next step
Session 8 on the 309 lane; first session of 804 (set it in-progress - owner-lane precedent: 304). The driver handed me the split parent again, not the subtask (804 was still not in Next-open-tasks after the iteration-98 dep fix); the parent's next step is its next subtask, so I worked 804 in my own lane (it is my subtask; the module fc67bb9 is on my branch - the Notes' wait rule applies only if a branch without the module received it).
1. Refactor first, per AGENTS.md: build() would exceed ~50 lines after the two-phase wiring and would gain the no-op branch, so this step extracted the entry construction into _entry() and restructured build() to gather the per-site candidate map first and derive the entries from that map - no behavior change, committed on its own. Evidence: the old build (git show HEAD:tools/fit_queue.py) and the new build, each run via the test's runpy guard on an identical temp tree (the four 305 inputs copied): both 116 entries, entries identical except `at`; test_fit_queue_synthetic and test_fit_queue_real pass unmodified (0.69 s).
2. The committed web/data/fit_queue.json is STALE vs current data: 117 entries, but the current data builds 116 - and the OLD build produces 116 too, so this is data drift, not a refactor artifact. The extra committed entry is shotwick-castle-q7502621 (no longer built from the current data; the same site is the orphan-platefit-doc behind the main-side failures test_serve::test_platefits_docs_match_sites and test_batch_eu). 805's rebuild absorbs it; 804 never writes the committed file. The earlier hand-overs' "117 entries" baseline is superseded: 116 is the current truth (the entry set and per-entry candidates of the 116 were re-derived and match the generator's output - that is test_fit_queue_real, passing).
3. New PITFALLS (Python 3.12.3): runpy.run_path does not put the script's own directory on sys.path (plain `python3 <script>` does; the test GUARDs run the tools' CLIs via runpy). Verified empirically this session: a sibling-module import in a runpy-run script fails with ModuleNotFoundError while the same script works under plain python3. Consequence for 804's wiring: tools/fit_queue.py must insert ROOT/tools (for right_place) and ROOT/fit (for review) into sys.path itself before the imports - exactly what tools/right_place.py's main() already does for fit_queue.
Next (iteration 100, same lane): 804 boxes 1+2 - the two-phase wiring in build() (_place_store/_place_flags/_apply_flags, full sketch in 804's hand-over; the no-op degrade keeps 305's synthetic tree green unmodified), verified against `python3 tools/right_place.py --all` (same 15 flags), then the box-4 tests and the box-3 README note; after that 805.
